title: Knossos: Minoan, Evans, or Copy?
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: A p5.js sorting activity in which learners place ten features of the palace of Knossos into three bins: Minoan originals still at the site, Arthur Evans's reconstructions of about 1905 to 1930, and modern copies of paintings whose originals are in the Heraklion Archaeological Museum.

learningObjectives: Distinguish surviving Minoan remains at Knossos from Arthur Evans's reconstructions and from modern copies of originals now in the Heraklion Archaeological Museum, sorting at least 8 of 10 features correctly on the first attempt.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Three-bin sorting with one scored attempt per card, immediate reasoned feedback, an optional material clue, and an unscored practice round
keyQuestions: Who made this: the Minoans, Evans, or a modern copyist?
What is this feature made of?
Where is the original of this painting today?
commonMisconceptions: Everything at Knossos that looks old is Minoan.
The bright red columns are original Minoan columns.
The wall paintings outdoors are the original frescoes.
Nothing at the site is original, so it is all fake.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score on ten cards (mastery: 8 of 10).
Explain why the red columns at the North Entrance are filed under Evans reconstruction.
On the day, photograph one feature from each bin with its label as evidence.
